issues: CSV export verification line format does not match the test expectations: the code should be a 76‑character string (first 12‑char hash of the CSV content concatenated with the headHash). In src/lib/exportCsv.ts the generated line uses "code=${code12}" only, omitting the headHash part, causing test M9 to get NaN for entryCount and failing to match the expected combined code length. Also the verification line format includes a "# verification:" prefix while the test expects just three comma‑separated values without the prefix, leading to parts length mismatch and wrong parsing.

Ledger entry creation for receipts and mileage does not record OCR pre‑fill data or the user‑confirmed data as required by R5–R7. The receipt store only appends receipt objects directly; there is no handling of OCR data, and the code does not differentiate between created and corrected data beyond the kind label, potentially missing required fields in data.

appendEntryForExport in src/lib/ledger.ts stores the export entry with a data object that has a "headHash" field set after computing the hash, but the verification line generated in exportCsv does not use this stored headHash; instead it recomputes a new hash from CSV content, causing inconsistency between the ledger entry and the verification line.

verifyLedger does not correctly detect missing entries when a later entry is missing (e.g., when a ledger entry is removed). The function checks for gaps after reconstructing the expected count from stored "ledgerSeqCount", but it never updates "ledgerSeqCount" after import of missing entries or after normal append operations, leading to false positives/negatives in some verification scenarios (R18–R20).

initLedgerIfNeeded in src/lib/ledgerHelpers.ts imports existing receipts and mileage as "imported" entries, but the timestamp "at" uses the current time for each entry, violating R11 which requires the import date to be recorded (the same import date for all imported entries). Also, it does not set a distinct "recordId" for mileage entries (it uses the same field but mileage records have different shape). This may cause duplicate imported entries or missing import of mileage entries (R12).

History screens (src/screens/ReceiptHistoryScreen.tsx, src/screens/MileageHistoryScreen.tsx) and UI components (HistoryItem, HistoryList) are present but not exported or integrated into navigation, and the UI flow (ui_flow.json) still points to the old screens. The UI flow test cannot find the "History" button, causing step 26 failures (R21–R24).

verifyExportCode in src/lib/exportVerification.ts only matches the 12‑character prefix of a verification code, ignoring the required concatenation with headHash. Hence it incorrectly reports codes as known when only the prefix matches, and fails to detect mismatched codes after export modifications (R32). It also does not recompute the verification code from a CSV file without the verification line, as required by R30.

Backup restore logic in src/lib/backup.ts verifies the ledger using verifyLedger(store, obj.ledger) but passes the current store (which still contains the old ledger) rather than the ledger data from the backup. This means verification is run on the wrong data, potentially allowing tampered backups to be restored without detection (R36–R37).

appendEntryForReceipt and appendEntryForMileage always append entries even when the store already contains a ledger, violating the append‑only model for ledger entries on “Delete all data” only (R13–R14). The “Delete all data” action does not clear the ledger, and there is no logic to reset the ledger on that action, leading to ledger entries persisting after a full data delete, contrary to R14.

CSV export verification line includes a "# verification:" prefix and labels (entries=, headHash=, code=) but tests expect a plain CSV line "<entryCount>,<headHash>,<verificationCode>" without labels. This mismatch causes test failures (M9).
feedback: The implementation of the tamper‑evident ledger and export verification does not meet the specification. CSV verification lines are formatted incorrectly, export codes are not concatenated with headHash, ledger import on first launch lacks a single import timestamp, and history UI integration is missing, causing UI flow tests to fail. Ledger verification does not correctly detect missing entries or handle ledger reset on full data deletion. Export verification does not recompute codes from CSV content or handle PDF codes correctly. Backup restore validates the wrong ledger data, allowing tampered backups. The code must be revised to conform to all listed requirements and to pass the acceptance tests.
